basis: official and allied sources; metadata links to original publications

records.name: Climate disruption & extreme weather
records.summary: WMO reports the past four years among the warmest on record. Increasing heat, storms and water stress interact with health, food systems, displacement and infrastructure.
records.triggers: Extreme heat, drought and flood exposure; El Niño conditions; failures of adaptation.

records.name: Nuclear escalation and strategic miscalculation
records.summary: A nuclear exchange would produce exceptional humanitarian consequences. The risk view does not assign a numerical probability or imply an imminent exchange.
records.triggers: Loss of crisis communication, mistaken warning, direct nuclear-armed power confrontation.

records.name: Major armed conflicts and civilian displacement
records.confidence: High for historical burden; future uncertain
records.summary: ACLED records widespread political violence. Humanitarian and cross-border spillovers differ by region; individual reports have their own event dates.
records.triggers: Escalation, regional intervention, growing civilian harm and loss of essential services.

records.name: Food and water insecurity
records.summary: FAO–WFP identify severe hunger hotspots. Conflict, drought, inflation and transport disruption may combine to deepen shortages.
records.triggers: Crop failures, blocked trade, drought, loss of aid and growing displacement.

records.name: Pandemic and biological risk
records.confidence: Low for timing; high for potential impact
records.summary: Outbreak emergence is not predictable to a date. WHO reports active emergencies and provides surveillance; this is a general preparedness risk, not a claim of imminent pandemic.
records.triggers: Disease spread, healthcare disruption, inadequate surveillance or response.

records.name: Energy chokepoint disruption
records.summary: EIA documents large oil and gas volumes moving through narrow maritime routes. Disruption can cascade into energy prices, fertilizer costs and food trade.
records.triggers: Shipping interruption, escalating regional fighting, damaged ports and insurance shocks.

records.name: Critical infrastructure cyber disruption
records.summary: CISA’s known exploited vulnerability catalog identifies exploitation, not necessarily a foreign government. Power, water and health system disruptions could cross sectors.
records.triggers: Coordinated attacks, exploited vulnerabilities and failure of critical backups.

records.name: Global financial and trade contagion
records.summary: Energy price shocks, supply chain bottlenecks and fiscal constraints can transmit across countries. No recession or crash date is asserted here.
records.triggers: Sudden credit tightening, trade blockade, major commodity price shock.

records.name: Biodiversity and ecosystem degradation
records.summary: IPCC identifies interacting risks to ecosystems, food, health and livelihoods, including possible irreversible impacts as warming increases.
records.triggers: Ecosystem loss, climate stress, habitat fragmentation and poor adaptation.

records.name: Disinformation, repression and institutional decay
records.summary: DOJ and historic declassified archives document examples of covert influence and espionage. A historical case is not proof a similar operation is active now.
records.triggers: Undisclosed influence networks, erosion of accountability, contested information.

records.name: AI misuse and information-system dependence
records.summary: Potential misuse and failures in increasingly automated systems could magnify cybersecurity, disinformation and infrastructure risks. This exploratory scenario is not a quantified existential forecast.
records.triggers: Security failures, scaled misuse, unsafe deployment and concentration of critical dependencies.
